sections.overview: The Sunda Pygmy Woodpecker is a very small resident of the Thai-Malay Peninsula, Borneo and the Sunda Islands; many current lists use Yungipicus moluccensis.
sections.identification: It has brown upperparts marked with white and pale, dark-streaked underparts; a red streak on the male’s hindcrown can be difficult to see.
sections.habitat: In Singapore, it uses coastal parks and gardens in urban areas.
sections.diet: It gleans and probes bark on slender dead branches and twigs for insects and other small invertebrates; it also forages on trees favored for food.
sections.behavior: It is usually encountered alone or in pairs and moves slowly while searching along bark and branches.
sections.reproduction: Like other woodpeckers, it nests in tree cavities; Singapore’s parks authority installed nest boxes because natural nesting holes can be limited.
sections.ecology: It can persist in modified urban landscapes where suitable trees remain.
sections.conservation: The Singapore Red Data Book lists the native species as Least Concern locally; that national category is not a substitute for a global assessment.
